question.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{22}\cdot {r}_{22}?$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns $\mathbf{q}_1,\mathbf{q}_2$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of $q_{12} \cdot r_{22}?$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct a matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2\mathbf{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by $Q^T,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14238290/assets/b1acf3e02d704f2d9b0a05536a35c5119aa04282de80d72c090a98d2d53ea971.svg)

Finally, $q_{12} \cdot r_{22} = -\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot 3 = -2.$
